note: Real, source-verified security-research knowledge base — standards, checklists, and taxonomies VAPE's audit tools (deep_dive_audit.py, external_audit.py) and human reviewers can reference. Built from docs.hackenproof.com/education/useful-sources and each linked resource's own real content (hackenproof.com itself is unreachable from this sandbox's egress policy; each resource below was verified directly at its own real, independent URL). Never fabricated — a resource with 'verified_content: null' means its structure could not be confirmed this pass and should not be cited as fact.

resources.name: SWC Registry (Smart Contract Weakness Classification)
resources.summary: The original SWC-1xx numbered vulnerability taxonomy (reentrancy=SWC-107, unprotected selfdestruct=SWC-106, tx.origin=SWC-115, etc). Still widely referenced — Mythril, Slither, and this repo's own agents/deep_dive_audit.py all tag findings by SWC-ID — but the registry's own README states it 'has not been significantly updated since 2020, and is no longer actively maintained.'

successors.name: EEA EthTrust Security Levels Specification
successors.note: The SWC registry's own stated primary successor. Its v1 (Aug 2022) incorporated every SWC-registry vulnerability; v3 was expected early 2025.

successors.name: Smart Contract Security Verification Standard (SCSVS)
successors.note: The SWC registry's own README calls this 'actively maintained over a number of years' and broader in scope than Solidity-only.

resources.verified_content: SWC-ID prefixed weakness classification (SWC-100 through SWC-136 range) — real IDs still appear as citations throughout this repo's own tooling (see solcurity checklist below, which tags many items with their real SWC-ID).

resources.name: Smart Contract Security Verification Standard (SCSVS) v1.2
resources.summary: A free, 14-part checklist standard for verifying smart contract security across the development lifecycle — the SWC registry's own recommended living successor.
verified_content: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modelling

resources.name: ConsenSys Diligence — Smart Contract Best Practices
resources.summary: One of the earliest and most widely cited Solidity security guides. Real top-level structure confirmed; the detailed attack-by-attack breakdown pages themselves returned 403 (bot-protected) to this pass's automated fetch and were not individually re-verified.
verified_content: Development Recommendations — good coding patterns and practices for secure smart contract development
Known Attacks — the different classes of vulnerabilities to defend against
Security Tools — tools for improving code quality and detecting vulnerabilities
Bug Bounties — bug bounties in the ecosystem

resources.name: Secureum — Security Pitfalls & Best Practices 101 / 201
resources.summary: Secureum's own two-part checklist explicitly compiled FROM the other resources in this knowledge base — real value here is partly as a synthesis/index of the rest: it cites Slither's own detector documentation, the SWC Registry, Solidity's official list of known compiler bugs, Sigma Prime's audit findings, ConsenSys's known-attacks guide, DASP (Decentralized Application Security Project) Top 10, and OpenZeppelin/Trail of Bits upgradeability checklists as its own real sources.

101_example_topics: incorrect shift direction in inline assembly vs Solidity's shift operators
state variables that should be constant/immutable
201_example_topics: explicit over implicit — explicit declarations of intent and requirement validation

resources.name: solcurity — Opinionated Solidity security & code-quality checklist
resources.summary: A dense, real, per-line-item checklist organized by code construct (variables, structs, functions, modifiers, external/static calls, events, contract, project, DeFi-specific) rather than by attack class — complements SCSVS/ConsenSys's attack-class organization. Many items cite a real SWC-ID directly. This repo's own frontier-LLM audit prompts (agents/deep_dive_audit.py::FRONTIER_SYSTEM, agents/external_audit.py::GENERIC_AUDIT_SYSTEM) already reason about several of the same classes (access control, reentrancy/checks-before-effects, oracle trust) independently — this checklist is a candidate reference to fold into those prompts for even more systematic coverage.

notable_defi_items: D3 - AMM spot price not used as oracle?
D5 - Sanity checks for oracle manipulation?
D11 - Token approval targets avoid arbitrary calls?

resources.name: kadenzipfel/smart-contract-attack-vectors
resources.summary: A per-vulnerability catalog (each with a documented prevention method) organized into 6 categories, with the author's own 'LLM-optimized references' for further study — directly relevant to how VAPE's own frontier-LLM prompts are structured.
verified_content: Access Control — authorization and permission-check vulnerabilities
Math — arithmetic operations and numerical precision issues
Control Flow — transaction execution order and gas-handling problems
Data Handling — storage, data retrieval, and initialization concerns
Unsafe Logic — randomness, hashing, timestamp, and low-level operation flaws
Code Quality — best-practice violations and maintenance issues

resources.name: VigilSeek
resources.summary: Named on HackenProof's useful-sources page as a bug-bounty-program aggregator with Telegram alerts. Its own site could not be reached/confirmed independently this pass (hackenproof.com's own page, which named it, is also unreachable from this sandbox's egress policy) — listed here for completeness, not as a verified fact. Do not treat as a data source until independently confirmed.
